question.worked_solution:
The definitions of $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{sinh}⁡x$ are

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x}),\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}).
$$

Substituting the above definitions into the equation $\operatorname{cosh}⁡x+\operatorname{sinh}⁡x=7,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}+{e}^{-x})+\frac{1}{2}({e}^{x}-{e}^{-x}) & =7 \\ \frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x}-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-x} & =7 \\ {e}^{x} & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & =7 \\ x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)$ is the only real solution to the equation.
